specification_compliance: I1/I10: service.py:830-900 adds the exact-match ids after the coarse ids. It drops ids that are already coarse, keeps only ids inside pre_scope when that is set, and builds scope_ids as the surviving coarse ids followed by the surviving exact-match ids. That scope_ids is passed as file_id_scope to every clue search (service.py:939). exact_match.py:96 extends the list in token order, sorted by file_id within a token, and skips duplicates.

I2: exact_match.py:20,39 skip a token shorter than 2 characters after quote removal. exact_match.py:92-95 skip a token that matches 0 files or more than max_files. _TABLES (exact_match.py:25-30) does not include fts_files*.

I3: exact_match.py:49-53 join indexed_files with i.drive = :drive AND i.active = 1 and use the column filter `text : "token"`. The text column exists in all four tables (app/database.py:1277-1314). service.py:842 applies pre_scope.

I4: service.py:853-855 sends the union to the access filter in a single call. service.py:887 and 896-898 keep only accessible ids. The SSE payload (service.py:1699-1710) is built from filtered_shortlist.
I5: exact_match.py:110 runs the lookup through asyncio.to_thread.
I6: service.py:911-918 fetch summaries for filtered_shortlist.file_ids only, which are the coarse ids in coarse order.

I7: exact_match.py:82-90 handle a failure on one table: that token is voided, a WARNING is logged, and the loop continues with the next token. exact_match.py:113-115 handle a total failure: () is returned and a WARNING is logged. No error event is sent.

I8: service.py:831 skips the lookup when the cap is 0. In that case exact_match_ids is empty, so the access-filter argument and scope_ids are the same as before the change. config.py:754-777 drop a value that is absent, null, negative, bool or not an int, so the dataclass default of 10 applies (config.py:356).

I9: the disabled/no-drive branch (service.py:745-757) and the small/empty/low-confidence branch (service.py:806-825) return before the lookup. The access-filter-empty branch (service.py:856-878) uses bypass_scope = pre_scope_file_ids.
potential_unspecified_behavior: The SQLite connection is reused for later tokens after one table raises (exact_match.py:75-90). For FTS5 syntax or missing-table errors SQLite keeps the connection usable. For other error classes I did not check whether a broken connection could make every later token fail too. This would still degrade safely to adding no files.
regression_risks: The clue-search scope can now be larger than coarse_top_k, by up to tokens × cap ids. The spec allows this, but it raises the size of the access-filter request and the scoped query.
test_coverage: tests/test_rag_shortlist_exact_match.py has dedicated SPEC-ADDON-035 tests for each invariant: ordering, the cap, the four tables, the text-column-only match, fts_files exclusion, drive and active filtering, pre_scope, access filtering, coarse-only clue input, top_score, every bypass branch, per-table and total failure, the event-loop check, and config validation.
